summary: Fixed blocker F-013 in apps/cli/src/commands/cli.ts by normalizing `--<declared string option> <value>` into the inline `--opt=value` form before parseArgs, which strict mode accepts even when the value begins with '-'. parseArgs keeps strict:true; the command allow-list, duplicate-token check, required-option check and exit-code contract are untouched. All 16 tests in cli.dashOptionValues.test.ts pass unmodified (was 10 failed / 6 passed), including the six over-correction guards. Full workspace pnpm test (7 projects; apps/cli 69 tests incl. 3 two-process E2E runs) and pnpm typecheck pass; no package declares a lint script. No test file was edited, skipped or deleted, and nothing was committed.
summary_markdown:
## What changed

One production file: `apps/cli/src/commands/cli.ts`.

- Added `inlineStringOptionValues(args)`, run over raw argv before `parseArgs`. It rewrites `--<declared string option> <value>` into `--<option>=<value>`; strict `parseArgs` accepts the inline form for a dash-leading value (`--to=-AbC` -> `-AbC`, `--text=--profile` -> `--profile`) while still throwing `ERR_PARSE_ARGS_UNKNOWN_OPTION` for an unknown flag.
- Added `stringOptions`, a `ReadonlySet` derived from `cliOptions` itself so the set cannot drift from the option table, and the `optionSeparator` constant.
- `strict: true`, `allowPositionals`, the `commandOptions` allow-list, the duplicate check over `parsed.tokens`, `rejectUnexpectedMissing`, `classify` and the 0/2/3/4/5 exit-code contract are unchanged.

## Why validation is not weakened

The rewrite is narrow, so every prior rejection path reaches the same code with the same argv shape:

- unknown flag (bare or with a dash value): name is not in `stringOptions`, nothing is rewritten or consumed, `parseArgs` still refuses it;
- missing value at end of argv: with no following argument there is nothing to inline, so `parseArgs` still reports the missing value (the normalizer never invents one, which is the trap since `parseArgs` uses the same error class for both);
- repeated option: `parseArgs` emits one option token per occurrence in either form, so the `seen` check is unaffected;
- option not allowed for the command, unknown command, stray positional: allow-list and positional handling untouched.

`strict: false` would have silenced the first, third and fourth of those; this fix cannot.

## Edge cases

- `--`: the scan stops at the first bare `--` and copies it plus everything after it verbatim. Bare trailing `--` stays a no-op (exit 0); any operand after `--` still becomes an unmatched positional (exit 2). An option immediately followed by `--` is passed through unchanged rather than taking `--` as a value.
- Booleans: `--json`/`--yes` are excluded by construction (filtered on `type === "string"`), so a boolean flag can never swallow the next argument — that is what keeps `doctor --json --profile` a missing-value error.
- Already-inline options: an argument containing `=` is passed through, so it is never re-wrapped and the next argument is not consumed. A value containing `=` survives because `parseArgs` splits on the first `=`.
- Applied uniformly rather than only to dash-leading values, so there is one code path; the forms are equivalent for `parseArgs` and `parseCommand` reads only `token.name`.

## Verification (all via `keryx ctx run`)

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| dash suite before | 10 failed, 6 passed (16) — RED confirmed |
| dash suite after | 16 passed (16), unmodified |
| `pnpm test` | all green: 7 projects; apps/cli 13 files / 69 tests incl. `test/e2e/two-process.test.ts` 3/3 |
| `pnpm typecheck` | pass (7 projects) |
| `pnpm lint` | no package declares a `lint` script |

No plaintext body, ciphertext, store key, private key material or HTTP request body reached any log or report; rejected argument values are not echoed into diagnostics.

acceptance.criterion: F-013 (blocker): every string-valued CLI option accepts a value beginning with '-'; a dash-leading value reaches its intended layer verbatim, and for --to that means the trust check (exit 3 CONTACT_NOT_TRUSTED), not the argument parser.
acceptance.evidence: All nine declared string options are covered by the now-green suite: --profile (exit 0), --relay-url and --store-key-env (exit 2 INVALID_CONFIGURATION from the config schema), --out and --from (exit 0), --to (exit 3 CONTACT_NOT_TRUSTED, byte-identical to the control run without the leading dash), --text (exit 3 CONTACT_NOT_TRUSTED), --message-id (exit 2 INVALID_MESSAGE_ID from the message-id validator), --with (exit 0 with an empty history).

acceptance.criterion: A --text value beginning with '-' is accepted as message content, including a flag-shaped value such as '--profile', and is never reinterpreted as an option.
acceptance.evidence: The trusted-send content test sends both '-SYNTHETIC_DASH_TEXT' and '--profile' over a stub relay (exit 0 each) and reads both back unchanged through history, proving neither value was reinterpreted or rewritten.

acceptance.criterion: Argument validation is NOT weakened: unknown flag (bare and with a dash value), missing value at end of argv, repeated option including a dash-leading repeat, option not allowed for the command, unknown command and stray positional all still fail closed with exit 2 INVALID_ARGUMENTS.
acceptance.evidence: parseArgs keeps strict:true; the normalizer only ever joins an argument that exists, only for names declared type:"string", and never for an argument already containing '='. The four guard tests covering these classes were passing before the change and still pass after it.

acceptance.criterion: The `--` separator behaviour pinned by the tests holds: a bare trailing `--` is a no-op with exit 0, and any operand after `--` fails closed with exit 2.
acceptance.evidence: The normalizer stops at the first bare '--' and copies the remainder verbatim, so positional handling is unchanged. Both separator tests pass.
16 passed (16). The test file was not opened for writing at any point; the only edit in this task is apps/cli/src/commands/cli.ts.

acceptance.criterion: The exit-code contract (0/2/3/4/5), the single-JSON-object-on-stdout rule and redacted stderr diagnostics are unchanged for every other case.
acceptance.evidence: classify(), writeResult() and main() are untouched. The pre-existing process-level suites cli.test.ts (6) and cli.processFailures.test.ts (8), which pin the exit-code map, the one-JSON-object rule and redaction, all still pass.

acceptance.criterion: The full apps/cli suite, `pnpm test` and `pnpm typecheck` pass, with no pre-existing test weakened, skipped or deleted.
acceptance.evidence: apps/cli: 13 test files / 69 tests passed, including test/e2e/two-process.test.ts 3/3. Workspace pnpm test green across all 7 projects; pnpm typecheck pass. No test file was modified.
